case_facts_html: Sun Limited has acquired 40% share in Moon Ltd. for ₹500,000 on 01.07.2023. Moon Ltd. is holding 40% stake in Star Limited. Now, sun limited can exercise significant influence on Moon Limited. Moon limited declared dividend of ₹80,000 for the Financial Year 2022-23 on 15.09.2023. For the year 2023-24, Moon Ltd. earned profit of ₹4,00,000 and declared dividend for ₹90,000 on 15.09.2024.
question_html: With respect to relationship between Companies, it can be said that:

options.A: Star Ltd. is associate of Sun Ltd.
options.B: Moon Ltd. and Star Ltd. both are associates of Sun Ltd.
options.C: Moon Ltd. is an associate of Sun Ltd.
options.D: Sun Ltd. is Parent of both Moon Ltd. and Star Ltd.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Moon Ltd. is an associate of Sun Ltd. — Sun's direct 40% stake in Moon falls within AS 23's significant-influence range (20%-50%), making Moon an associate. Star Ltd. is not itself directly held by Sun; Moon's 40% stake in Star does not, on its own, extend associate status from Sun to Star, since Moon is only an associate (not a subsidiary) of Sun, and AS 23 does not treat an indirect holding routed through another associate as conferring significant influence.
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.3): Associate relationship via direct significant influence; an indirect stake held through another associate does not itself confer associate status

case_facts_html: Sun Limited has acquired 40% share in Moon Ltd. for ₹500,000 on 01.07.2023. Moon Ltd. is holding 40% stake in Star Limited. Now, sun limited can exercise significant influence on Moon Limited. Moon limited declared dividend of ₹80,000 for the Financial Year 2022-23 on 15.09.2023. For the year 2023-24, Moon Ltd. earned profit of ₹4,00,000 and declared dividend for ₹90,000 on 15.09.2024.
question_html: What will be the carrying amount of investment in Consolidated Financial Statements of Sun Limited as on 31.03.2024?
answer_html: Answer: (B) ₹5,88,000 — under the equity method for CFS, the carrying amount starts from the same pre-acquisition-dividend-adjusted cost as the separate financial statements (₹4,68,000, see Q3(b)) and is increased by Sun's 40% share of Moon's post-acquisition profit for FY2023-24, time-apportioned for the 9 months since acquisition (01.07.2023 to 31.03.2024): 40% × ₹4,00,000 × 9/12 = ₹1,20,000. Carrying amount = ₹4,68,000 + ₹1,20,000 = ₹5,88,000.
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.6): Equity-method carrying amount: cost net of pre-acquisition dividend plus a time-apportioned share of post-acquisition profit

case_facts_html: Sun Limited has acquired 40% share in Moon Ltd. for ₹500,000 on 01.07.2023. Moon Ltd. is holding 40% stake in Star Limited. Now, sun limited can exercise significant influence on Moon Limited. Moon limited declared dividend of ₹80,000 for the Financial Year 2022-23 on 15.09.2023. For the year 2023-24, Moon Ltd. earned profit of ₹4,00,000 and declared dividend for ₹90,000 on 15.09.2024.
question_html: As per AS 23, the existence of significant influence by an investor is usually evidenced in one or more of the following ways: (a) participation in policy making processes; (b) interchange of managerial personnel; (c) right to receive dividend; (d) provision of essential technical information.
answer_html: Answer: (D) Statements (a), (b) and (d) are correct — participation in policy-making, interchange of managerial personnel, and provision of essential technical information are all AS 23 evidences of significant influence. A mere right to receive dividend (statement c) is not, since it is a passive entitlement common to any shareholder rather than evidence of participation in decisions.
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.3): Evidences of significant influence under AS 23 - excludes a mere right to receive dividend

case_facts_html:
Sun Limited has acquired 40% share in Moon Ltd. for ₹5,00,000 on 01.07.2024. Moon Ltd. is holding 40% stake in Star Limited. Sun Limited can exercise significant influence on Moon Limited. Moon Limited declared dividend of ₹80,000 for FY 2023-24 on 15.09.2024. For 2024-25, Moon Ltd. earned profit of ₹4,00,000 and declared dividend of ₹90,000 on 15.09.2025.

Answer the following questions based on the above.
question_html: With respect to relationship between Companies, it can be said that:

options.A: Star Ltd. is associate of Sun Ltd.
options.B: Moon Ltd. and Star Ltd. both are associates of Sun Ltd.
options.C: Moon Ltd. is an associate of Sun Ltd.
options.D: Sun Ltd. is Parent of both Moon Ltd. and Star Ltd.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Moon Ltd. is an associate of Sun Ltd. — Sun Ltd. holds 40% (≥20%) of Moon Ltd. with significant influence, making Moon an associate. Star Ltd. is held only indirectly, through Moon (which is itself merely an associate, not a subsidiary, of Sun) — AS 23's associate-via-subsidiary attribution logic does not extend through a non-controlled intermediate, so Star Ltd. is not Sun Ltd.'s associate on these facts.
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.2): Associate relationship does not extend through a non-controlled intermediate holding

case_facts_html:
Sun Limited has acquired 40% share in Moon Ltd. for ₹5,00,000 on 01.07.2024. Moon Ltd. is holding 40% stake in Star Limited. Sun Limited can exercise significant influence on Moon Limited. Moon Limited declared dividend of ₹80,000 for FY 2023-24 on 15.09.2024. For 2024-25, Moon Ltd. earned profit of ₹4,00,000 and declared dividend of ₹90,000 on 15.09.2025.

Answer the following questions based on the above.
question_html: What will be the carrying amount of investment in Consolidated Financial Statements of Sun Limited as on 31.03.2025?
answer_html: Answer: (B) ₹5,88,000 — equity method: cost ₹5,00,000, plus 40% share of Moon's FY2024-25 post-acquisition profit for the 9 months held (01.07.2024–31.03.2025): ₹4,00,000 × 9/12 × 40% = ₹1,20,000, less the pre-acquisition-period dividend received (declared 15.09.2024 out of FY2023-24 profit, predating the 01.07.2024 acquisition) — 40% × ₹80,000 = ₹32,000 deducted under the equity method regardless of the dividend's profit-source period. Net: 5,00,000 + 1,20,000 − 32,000 = ₹5,88,000.
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.6): Equity method - time-apportioned post-acquisition profit share, less dividends received

case_facts_html:
Sun Limited has acquired 40% share in Moon Ltd. for ₹5,00,000 on 01.07.2024. Moon Ltd. is holding 40% stake in Star Limited. Sun Limited can exercise significant influence on Moon Limited. Moon Limited declared dividend of ₹80,000 for FY 2023-24 on 15.09.2024. For 2024-25, Moon Ltd. earned profit of ₹4,00,000 and declared dividend of ₹90,000 on 15.09.2025.

Answer the following questions based on the above.
question_html: As per AS 23, the existence of significant influence by an investor is usually evidenced in one or more of the following ways: (i) Participation in policy making processes; (ii) Interchange of managerial personnel; (iii) Right to receive dividend; (iv) Provision of essential technical information.
answer_html: Answer: (D) — AS 23 lists board representation, policy-making participation, material inter-company transactions, interchange of managerial personnel, and provision of essential technical information as significant-influence indicators. "Right to receive dividend" (iii) is a basic shareholder right held by any investor, however small the stake, and is not itself evidence of significant influence.

case_facts_html:
SEAS Ltd., the "Company", is in the business of tours and travels. It sells holiday packages to the customers. The Company negotiates upfront with the Airlines for specified number of seats in flight. The Company agrees to buy a specific number of tickets and pay for those tickets regardless of whether it is able to resell all of those in package.

The rate paid by the Company for each ticket purchased is negotiated and agreed in advance. The Company also assists the customers in resolving complaints with the service provided by airlines. However, each airline is responsible for fulfilling obligations associated with the ticket, including remedies to a customer for dissatisfaction with the service.

The Company bought a forward contract for three months of US$ 1,00,000 on 1 March 2024 at 1 US$ = INR 83.10 when exchange rate was US$ 1 = INR 83.02. On 31 March 2024, when the Company closed its books, exchange rate was US$ 1 = INR 83.15. On 1 April 2024, the Company decided for premature settlement of the contract due to some exceptional circumstances.

The Company is evaluating below mentioned schemes: (i) Introduction of a formal retirement gratuity scheme by an employer in place of ad hoc ex-gratia payments to employees on retirement. (ii) Management decided to pay pension to those employees who have retired after completing 5 years of service in the organization. Such employees will get pension of ₹20,000 per month. Earlier there was no such scheme of pension in the organization.

SEAS Ltd. has a subsidiary, ADI Ltd., which is in the business of construction having turnover of ₹200 crores. SEAS Ltd. and ADI Ltd. hold 9% and 23% respectively in an associate company, ASOC Ltd. Both SEAS Ltd. and ADI Ltd. prepare consolidated financial statements as per Accounting Standards notified under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021.
question_html: Please comment regarding consolidation requirements for SEAS Ltd. and ADI Ltd. using the below mentioned options as to which one should be correct.

options.A: ADI Ltd. would use equity method of accounting for 23% in ASOC Ltd. SEAS Ltd. would consolidate ADI Ltd. and consequently automatically equity account 23% and separately account for the balance 9% as per AS 13.
options.B: ADI Ltd. would account for 23% in ASOC Ltd. as per AS 13. SEAS Ltd. would consolidate ADI Ltd. and consequently automatically account 23% and separately account for the balance 9%.
options.C: ADI Ltd. would account for 23% share in ASOC Ltd. using equity method of accounting. SEAS Ltd. would consolidate ADI Ltd. and consequently, automatically account for ASOC Ltd. 23% share and separately account for 9% share in ASOC Ltd. using equity method of accounting in consolidated financial statements.
options.D: ADI Ltd. would account for 23% in ASOC Ltd. as per AS 13. SEAS Ltd. would consolidate ADI Ltd. and using equity method of accounting 23% in ASOC Ltd. and separately account for the balance 9% as per AS 13.

answer_html: Answer: (C) — ADI Ltd.'s own 23% direct stake already exceeds the 20% significant-influence threshold, so ADI Ltd. equity-accounts it under AS 23 in its own books; when SEAS Ltd. consolidates its subsidiary ADI Ltd. under AS 21, that 23% equity-accounted stake carries through automatically. Separately, at the group level SEAS Ltd.'s own direct 9% is not tested in isolation — the group's combined effective interest (direct 9% + indirect 23% via the subsidiary = 32%) exceeds 20%, so ASOC Ltd. is an associate of the group as a whole, and SEAS Ltd.'s direct 9% must also be equity-accounted (not treated as a plain AS 13 investment), consistent with AS 23's rule on aggregating direct and indirect holdings through a controlled subsidiary.
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.3): Effective direct-plus-indirect associate holding through an intermediate/controlled subsidiary, tested at the group level

case_facts_html:
ADI Ltd (the Company), engaged in the business of manufacturing of urea, has set up its business in a designated backward area which entitles the company to receive from the Government of India a subsidy of 20% of the cost of investment.

Having fulfilled all the conditions under the scheme, the Company on its overall investment of ₹50 crores received ₹10 crores from the Government in January 2024 (financial year being 2023-24). The Company wants to treat this receipt as an item of revenue and thereby reduce the losses on profit and loss account for the year ended 31 March 2024.

ADI Ltd holds 51% in SHA Ltd. SHA Ltd is a joint venture of ADI Ltd due to a contractual agreement. ADI Ltd is engaged in the manufacturing business and it entered into a joint venture to get synergies in the same business. ADI Ltd and SHA Ltd hold 10% and 30% respectively in SHB Ltd.

As per the requirements of SEBI, ADI Ltd prepared results/accounts for the quarter ended 30 June 2024 and took following positions in respect of following accounting matters:

  1. Training expenses incurred during the quarter ended 30 June 2024 were allocated equally over the four quarters because the benefit was spread over the entire year and similarly some training expenses expected to be incurred in the last quarter have been estimated and equally allocated over the four quarters.
  2. Provision made for donation of ₹5 million expected to be made in the second quarter.
  3. Since historically there has been an immaterial variance between budgets and actuals, depreciation charge for the quarter was determined by the budgeted figure.
  4. Incentives were provided to the customers if they purchase 1 million kgs of urea on an annual basis. It was expected that at least 50 customers would be able to achieve this target before the end of third quarter. No provision was made for this incentive during the quarter ended 30 June 2024 since ADI Ltd believed that the provision was not yet fructified.

ADI Ltd owns 60% holding in ANI Ltd, an unquoted entity. The government has recently announced an increase in interest rates. The increase will cause a fall in value of equity holdings. This is due to the fact that risk free investments offer a higher return making them relatively more attractive. The market value of equity will adjust downwards to improve the return available on this sort of investment.

SHB Ltd took a loan of USD 10,000 on 1 April 2023 for a specific project at an interest rate of 5% p.a. payable annually. On 1 April 2023, the exchange rate between the currency was ₹81 per USD. The exchange rate as at 31 March 2024 was ₹82 per USD. The corresponding amount could have been borrowed by SHB Ltd in local currency at an interest rate of 11% per annum as on 1 April 2023.

ADI Ltd follows April to March as the financial year.
question_html: Please suggest which one of the following options would be correct in respect of consolidated accounts of ADI Ltd as per Accounting Standards notified under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules.

options.A: In the consolidated accounts of ADI Ltd, it would account for its 10% investment in SHB Ltd as per AS 13 and 30% investment of SHA Ltd in SHB Ltd would be accounted for using equity method.
options.B: In the consolidated accounts of ADI Ltd, it would account for its 10% investment in SHB Ltd as per equity method and 30% investment of SHA Ltd in SHB Ltd would be accounted using proportionate consolidation method.
options.C: In the consolidated accounts of ADI Ltd, it would account for its 10% investment in SHB Ltd as per AS 13 and 30% investment of SHA Ltd in SHB Ltd would be accounted using proportionate consolidation method.
options.D: In the consolidated accounts of ADI Ltd, it would account for its 10% investment in SHB Ltd as per equity method and 30% investment of SHA Ltd in SHB Ltd would also be accounted for using equity method.

answer_html: Answer: (D) — at the ADI Group's consolidated level, ADI's own direct 10% stake and SHA's 30% stake in SHB Ltd represent a single reporting entity's combined ownership interest in SHB (10% + 51% economic interest in SHA's 30% ≈ 25%+ effective exposure), which crosses the 20% significant-influence threshold in aggregate, with SHA's board seats and business synergies giving the wider group real participation in SHB's policy decisions. On that basis, SHB is treated as an associate of the ADI Group as a whole and equity-accounted for both stakes in the consolidated statements.
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.3): Group's combined direct and indirect (through a jointly-controlled entity) interest assessed together for significant influence in consolidated accounts

case_facts_html:
P Limited took a loan of USD 1,00,000 on 1st April, 2024 for a specific project at 5% p.a., payable annually. Exchange rate 1st April, 2024: ₹75/USD; 31st March, 2025: ₹80/USD. The equivalent amount could have been borrowed locally at 10% p.a.

P Limited holds 12% of the voting shares in G Limited. G Limited's board comprises eight members, two of whom are appointed by P Limited, casting significant influence.

P Limited manufactures toys at Muzaffarnagar: Material Cost ₹200/unit, Direct Labour ₹40/unit, Direct Variable Production Overheads ₹20/unit. Plant capacity 1,00,000 units p.a.; fixed production overheads ₹15,00,000 p.a. Actual production 2024-25: 1,20,000 units. 11,000 units of finished toys unsold at year end.

P Limited also renders catering services. At a 2024-25 wedding it catered, ten people died possibly from food poisoning. Legal proceedings seek ₹10,00,000 compensation; P Limited disputes liability. Legal counsel advises the company is likely to lose, though chances of paying the claim are not remote. Estimated: (i) legal cost ₹75,000 (irrespective of outcome); (ii) settlement if claim paid ₹10,00,000.

Based on the information given above, answer Question Nos. 1–5.
question_html: What is the relationship of G Limited with P Limited as per the relevant Accounting Standard?

options.A: G Limited is a subsidiary of P Limited.
options.B: G Limited is an associate of P Limited.
options.C: G Limited is a Joint Venture of P Limited.
options.D: P Limited has invested in G Limited with no further relationship as subsidiary, associate or joint venture.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Associate — despite holding only 12% of voting shares, P Limited has significant influence via board representation (2 of 8 board seats), which AS 23 treats as evidence of significant influence independent of the 20% voting-power presumption.
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.3): Significant influence evidenced by board representation, even below the 20% voting-power threshold

case_facts_html:
V Limited contracted to construct a hostel for MR College at ₹224 lakhs on 1st October, 2024 (expected completion 18 months). Cost incurred to 31st March, 2025: ₹60 lakhs. Prudent estimate of additional cost for completion: ₹180 lakhs. Billed to MR College: ₹84 lakhs.

On 1st June, 2024, V Limited acquired 30% of M Limited for ₹20,00,000, gaining significant influence. On 14th August, 2024, M Limited declared a dividend of ₹5,00,000 out of its FY2023-24 profit of ₹8,00,000. M Limited earned ₹30,00,000 for FY2024-25 (profits accrue evenly) and declared a dividend of ₹6,00,000 on 15th June, 2025.

V Limited's pre-tax profit: Q1 FY2024-25 ₹7,00,000, Q2 ₹8,00,000, expected Q3 ₹4,00,000, Q4 ₹6,00,000. Corporate tax slab: 30% on first ₹5,00,000, 40% on additional earnings.

Deferred tax information as at 31st March, 2025: Depreciation per accounting records ₹4,00,000; Depreciation allowable under Section 32 of the Income Tax Act ₹10,00,000; Unamortized Preliminary Expenses per tax records ₹30,000; GST penalty imposed 30th March, 2025, payable 30th April, 2025, ₹1,25,000.

Based on the information given above, answer Question Nos. 6–9.
question_html: What would be the carrying amount of Investment in M Limited in the Consolidated Financial Statements of V Limited as at 31st March, 2025?
answer_html: Answer: (B) ₹26,00,000 — under the equity method: cost ₹20,00,000, plus V Limited's 30% share of M Limited's post-acquisition-period profit (M's FY2024-25 profit of ₹30,00,000 accrues evenly over the year; V held the investment for 10 of the 12 months, 1st June 2024 to 31st March 2025, so the relevant share is ₹30,00,000 × 10/12 × 30% = ₹7,50,000), less the dividend received during the holding period (the ₹5,00,000 dividend declared 14th August 2024, of which V's 30% share = ₹1,50,000). Total: ₹20,00,000 + ₹7,50,000 − ₹1,50,000 = ₹26,00,000. The dividend reduces the carrying amount either way under the equity method — unlike the cost method, whether it was declared out of pre- or post-acquisition profit does not change this: the equity method already picks up the investor's share of the investee's profit as it is earned, so a dividend received is simply a cash realisation of value already reflected in the carrying amount, and always reduces it. (The later 15th June 2025 dividend is after the balance sheet date and irrelevant here.)
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.6): Equity method - carrying amount adjusted for investor's share of post-acquisition profit (time-apportioned) and always reduced by dividends received, regardless of pre/post-acquisition profit source

case_facts_html:
Road Builders Corp. is a publicly traded infrastructure and commercial real estate development company. On 1st April, 2025, it: (1) acquired 200 acres of land at ₹35,000 per acre for a new equipment yard and fabrication facility; (2) purchased machinery costing ₹320 Lakhs for a construction project in a backward area, immediately receiving a Government Grant of ₹80 Lakhs (company policy: deduct grant from cost of asset); estimated useful life 10 years, salvage value ₹6 Lakhs, straight line depreciation.

Road Builders Corp. acquired equity stakes in GeoSurvey Limited: 1st April, 2025 – 10% stake for ₹40,00,000; 1st October, 2025 – a further 15% stake for ₹58,00,000, reaching 25% total and gaining significant influence. GeoSurvey's net assets (book value): ₹3,40,00,000 on 1st April, 2025; ₹4,00,00,000 on 1st October, 2025.

On 1st April, 2025, Road Builders Corp. undertook a contract to construct an underpass. For the year ended 31st March, 2026: Total Contract Price ₹1,02,00,000; Cost Incurred till 31st March, 2026 ₹77,98,800; Prudent estimate of additional cost for completion ₹38,41,200.

Road Builders Corp. is also developing a shopping mall (expected complete end of March 2026, inauguration planned 1st April 2026), within which a Multiplex theatre was completed earlier, on 1st February, 2026. The company had a 'soft opening' of the theatre: tickets sold at 50% discount, theatre operating at 70% capacity; management claims this soft opening is a trial run necessary to check operational capability and system integration for the entire mall complex.

Based on the information given in the above case scenario, answer Question Nos. 1–4.
question_html: What is the amount of goodwill or capital reserve arising when RoadBuilders Corp. achieves significant influence in GeoSurvey Limited?
chapter_label: AS 23: Accounting for Investments in Associates in CFS
topic_text: AS 23 (2.6): Step acquisition to significant influence - goodwill/capital reserve computed on the tranche that achieves significant influence
